parse.title: Spirituality intensification
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>
'''Spirituality intensification''' is defined as the experience of a shift in a person’s personal beliefs regarding their existence and place within the universe, their relationship to others, and what they value as meaningful in life. It results in a person rethinking the significance they place on certain key concepts, holding some in higher regard than they did previously, and dismissing others as less important.<ref name="LSD-life-threatening-anxiety">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Gasser, P.)), ((Kirchner, K.)), ((Passie, T.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=LSD-assisted psychotherapy for anxiety associated with a life-threatening disease: A qualitative study of acute and sustained subjective effects | volume=29 | issue=1 | pages=57–68 | date= January 2015 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881114555249 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881114555249}}</ref> These concepts and notions are not limited to but generally include:

*An increased sense of personal purpose.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Peterman, A. H.)), ((Fitchett, G.)), ((Brady, M. J.)), ((Hernandez, L.)), ((Cella, D.)) | journal=Annals of Behavioral Medicine | title=Measuring spiritual well-being in people with cancer: The functional assessment of chronic illness therapy—spiritual well-being scale (FACIT-Sp) | volume=24 | issue=1 | pages=49–58 | date= February 2002 | url=https://academic.oup.com/abm/article/24/1/49-58/4631552 | issn=0883-6612 | doi=10.1207/S15324796ABM2401_06}}</ref>
*An increased interest in the pursuit of developing personal religious and spiritual ideologies.<ref name="ayahuasca-spirituality">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Trichter, S.)), ((Klimo, J.)), ((Krippner, S.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Changes in Spirituality Among Ayahuasca Ceremony Novice Participants | volume=41 | issue=2 | pages=121–134 | date= June 2009 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02791072.2009.10399905 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2009.10399905}}</ref><ref name="psilo-persisting-effects">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Griffiths, R. R.)), ((Johnson, M. W.)), ((Richards, W. A.)), ((Richards, B. D.)), ((McCann, U.)), ((Jesse, R.)) | journal=Psychopharmacology | title=Psilocybin occasioned mystical-type experiences: immediate and persisting dose-related effects | volume=218 | issue=4 | pages=649–665 | date= December 2011 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00213-011-2358-5 | issn=0033-3158 | doi=10.1007/s00213-011-2358-5}}</ref>
**The formation of complex personal religious beliefs.
*An increased sense of compassion towards nature and other people.<ref name="ayahuasca-spirituality" /><ref name="psilo-persisting-effects" /><ref name="values-psych-users">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Lerner, M.)), ((Lyvers, M.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Values and Beliefs of Psychedelic Drug Users: A Cross-Cultural Study | volume=38 | issue=2 | pages=143–147 | date= June 2006 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02791072.2006.10399838 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2006.10399838}}</ref>
*An increased sense of [[Unity and interconnectedness|unity and interconnectedness]] between oneself, nature, "god", and the universe as a whole.<ref name="LSD-life-threatening-anxiety" /><ref name="ayahuasca-spirituality" /><ref name="values-psych-users" /><ref name="psiloMYST">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Griffiths, R. R.)), ((Richards, W. A.)), ((McCann, U.)), ((Jesse, R.)) | journal=Psychopharmacology | title=Psilocybin can occasion mystical-type experiences having substantial and sustained personal meaning and spiritual significance | volume=187 | issue=3 | pages=268–283 | date= August 2006 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00213-006-0457-5 | issn=0033-3158 | doi=10.1007/s00213-006-0457-5}}</ref><ref name="psilo-openness">{{cite journal | vauthors=((MacLean, K. A.)), ((Johnson, M. W.)), ((Griffiths, R. R.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=Mystical experiences occasioned by the hallucinogen psilocybin lead to increases in the personality domain of openness | volume=25 | issue=11 | pages=1453–1461 | date= November 2011 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881111420188 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881111420188}}</ref><ref name="psilo-neuronal-oscillations">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Kometer, M.)), ((Pokorny, T.)), ((Seifritz, E.)), ((Volleinweider, F. X.)) | journal=Psychopharmacology | title=Psilocybin-induced spiritual experiences and insightfulness are associated with synchronization of neuronal oscillations | volume=232 | issue=19 | pages=3663–3676 | date= October 2015 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00213-015-4026-7 | issn=0033-3158 | doi=10.1007/s00213-015-4026-7}}</ref><ref name="illicit-use-of-lsd">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Lyvers, M.)), ((Meester, M.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Illicit Use of LSD or Psilocybin, but not MDMA or Nonpsychedelic Drugs, is Associated with Mystical Experiences in a Dose-Dependent Manner | volume=44 | issue=5 | pages=410–417 | date=1 November 2012 | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02791072.2012.736842 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2012.736842}}</ref>
*A decreased sense of value placed upon money and material objects.<ref name="values-psych-users" />
*A decreased fear and greater acceptance of death and the finite nature of existence.<ref name="LSD-life-threatening-anxiety" /><ref name="psilo-anxiety/depression-reduction">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ross, S.)), ((Bossis, A.)), ((Guss, J.)), ((Agin-Liebes, G.)), ((Malone, T.)), ((Cohen, B.)), ((Mennenga, S. E.)), ((Belser, A.)), ((Kalliontzi, K.)), ((Babb, J.)), ((Su, Z.)), ((Corby, P.)), ((Schmidt, B. L.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=Rapid and sustained symptom reduction following psilocybin treatment for anxiety and depression in patients with life-threatening cancer: a randomized controlled trial | volume=30 | issue=12 | pages=1165–1180 | date= December 2016 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881116675512 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881116675512}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Grob, C. S.)), ((Danforth, A. L.)), ((Chopra, G. S.)), ((Hagerty, M.)), ((McKay, C. R.)), ((Halberstadt, A. L.)), ((Greer, G. R.)) | journal=Archives of General Psychiatry | title=Pilot Study of Psilocybin Treatment for Anxiety in Patients With Advanced-Stage Cancer | volume=68 | issue=1 | pages=71 | date=3 January 2011 | url=http://archpsyc.jamanetwork.com/article.aspx?doi=10.1001/archgenpsychiatry.2010.116 | issn=0003-990X | doi=10.1001/archgenpsychiatry.2010.116}}</ref>

Although difficult to fully specify due to the subjective aspect of spirituality intensification, these changes in to a person's belief system can often result in profound changes in a person's personality<ref name="values-psych-users" /><ref name="psilo-openness" /><ref name="acute-subacute-long-psilo">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Studerus, E.)), ((Kometer, M.)), ((Hasler, F.)), ((Vollenweider, F. X.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=Acute, subacute and long-term subjective effects of psilocybin in healthy humans: a pooled analysis of experimental studies | volume=25 | issue=11 | pages=1434–1452 | date= November 2011 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881110382466 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881110382466}}</ref> which can sometimes be distinctively noticeable to the people around those who undergo it. This shift can occur suddenly but will usually increase gradually over time as a person repeatedly uses the [[psychoactive substance]] which is inducing it.

Spirituality intensification is unlikely to be an isolated effect component but rather the result of a combination of an appropriate setting<ref name="ayahuasca-spirituality" /> in conjunction with other coinciding effects such as [[analysis enhancement]], [[autonomous voice communication]], [[novelty enhancement]], [[perception of interdependent opposites]], [[perception of predeterminism]], [[perception of self-design]], [[personal bias suppression]], and [[unity and interconnectedness]]. It is most commonly induced under the influence of [[dosage#common|moderate]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[psychedelic]] compounds, such as [[LSD]], [[psilocybin]], and [[mescaline]]. However, it can also occur to a lesser extent under the influence of [[dissociative|dissociatives]], such as [[ketamine]], [[PCP]], and [[DXM]].
</onlyinclude>

====Analysis====
There have been a number of in-depth scientific studies which unanimously support the legitimate existence of the spiritual effects induced by [[hallucinogen]] usage.<ref name="LSD-life-threatening-anxiety" /><ref name="ayahuasca-spirituality" /><ref name="psilo-persisting-effects" /><ref name="values-psych-users" /><ref name="psiloMYST" /><ref name="psilo-openness" /><ref name="psilo-neuronal-oscillations" /><ref name="illicit-use-of-lsd" /><ref name="acute-subacute-long-psilo" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Cummins, C.)), ((Lyke, J.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Peak Experiences of Psilocybin Users and Non-Users | volume=45 | issue=2 | pages=189–194 | date= April 2013 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02791072.2013.785855 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2013.785855}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Griffiths, R.)), ((Richards, W.)), ((Johnson, M.)), ((McCann, U.)), ((Jesse, R.)) | journal=Journal of Psychopharmacology | title=Mystical-type experiences occasioned by psilocybin mediate the attribution of personal meaning and spiritual significance 14 months later | volume=22 | issue=6 | pages=621–632 | date= August 2008 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881108094300 | issn=0269-8811 | doi=10.1177/0269881108094300}}</ref><ref name="attitudes-to-drug-induced-religious">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bakalar, J. B.)) | journal=Journal of Humanistic Psychology | title=Social and Intellectual Attitudes Toward Drug-Induced Religious Experience | volume=25 | issue=4 | pages=45–66 | date= October 1985 | url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0022167885254008 | issn=0022-1678 | doi=10.1177/0022167885254008}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Móró, L.)), ((Simon, K.)), ((Bárd, I.)), ((Rácz, J.)) | journal=Journal of Psychoactive Drugs | title=Voice of the Psychonauts: Coping, Life Purpose, and Spirituality in Psychedelic Drug Users | volume=43 | issue=3 | pages=188–198 | date= July 2011 | url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/02791072.2011.605661 | issn=0279-1072 | doi=10.1080/02791072.2011.605661}}</ref><ref name="psych-pharm-review">{{cite journal | vauthors=((Nichols, D.  </onlyinclude>
Frequently, new [[psychedelic]] users rate their experience to be either the single most meaningful experience of their life or among the top five most meaningful experiences of their life.<ref name="psilo-persisting-effects" /><ref name="psiloMYST" /><ref name="psilo-anxiety/depression-reduction" /><ref name="acute-subacute-long-psilo" />

Any [[psychedelic]] or [[hallucinogen]] intentionally used for religious or spiritual purposes is known in the literature as an [[entheogen]].<ref name="ayahuasca-spirituality" /><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ruck, C.
